title: Harden accepted.toml mutations: reject nameless waive, atomic write, file lock
description:
Three related robustness gaps in the accepted.toml mutation path (surfaced by vidhi-review of sutra/303+308):

1. **Waiving a nameless constraint silently produces an inert entry.** `accepted_key()` falls back to constraint_id when name is None. `resolve_ref()` matches by name only, so the entry resolves as Unknown on the next load — the waiver never takes effect but `handle_waive` returns success. Fix: reject at handle_waive entry with a clear error telling the user to name the constraint.

2. **Non-atomic file write.** `write_accepted_file` does `std::fs::write` (O_TRUNC + write). Crash mid-write → truncated/corrupt source of truth, blocks all operations until manual repair. Fix: write to `.sutra/accepted.toml.tmp` then `fs::rename` (atomic on same filesystem).

3. **No file-level lock on read-modify-write.** upsert/remove functions do load→modify→write with no flock. Two concurrent calls can produce a lost update. The codebase already has `acquire_parse_flock` in pipeline.rs. Fix: advisory flock around the load/mutate/write span. Pairs naturally with the atomic write.

Bonus: batch handle_baseline's N upsert_ack calls into one file write cycle instead of N."

acceptance_criteria.text: handle_waive returns an error (not success) when the resolved constraint has no name
File mutations (upsert_waiver, remove_waiver, upsert_ack, remove_ack) hold an advisory flock
handle_baseline does one file write for all ack entries, not N
